## Proof

**Step 1: Cardinality of $P$.**

Each element of $P$ is an open interval $(a,b)$ determined by its two endpoints $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. The map $(a,b) \mapsto (a,b)$ identifies $P$ with a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ (namely $\{(a,b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : a < b\}$, but even without the inequality constraint the parameter space is $\mathbb{R}^2$). Since $|\mathbb{R}^2| = |\mathbb{R}| = C$, we have
$$|P| = C.$$

**Step 2: Upper bound on $|Q|$.**

A countable union of elements of $P$ is determined by a countable sequence $(I_1, I_2, I_3, \dots)$ with each $I_n \in P$ (finite unions are included by repeating an element or allowing the sequence to eventually be empty — in any case finite sequences are absorbed into countable ones). The set of all such sequences is $P^{\mathbb{N}}$, whose cardinality is
$$|P^{\mathbb{N}}| = |P|^{\aleph_0} = C^{\aleph_0} = (2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0 \cdot \aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0} = C.$$

The map $(I_1, I_2, \dots) \mapsto \bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty} I_n$ is a surjection from $P^{\mathbb{N}}$ onto $Q$, since every countable union arises from some such sequence. Therefore
$$|Q| \leq |P^{\mathbb{N}}| = C.$$

**Step 3: Lower bound on $|Q|$.**

Every single interval $(a,b) \in P$ is itself a countable union (the union of the one-element family $\{(a,b)\}$). Hence $P \subseteq Q$, which gives
$$|Q| \geq |P| = C.$$

**Step 4: Conclusion.**

Combining the upper and lower bounds:
$$C \leq |Q| \leq C,$$
so by the Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein theorem,
$$|Q| = C.$$

The cardinality of $Q$ is equal to the cardinality of the continuum.
